proposals.evidence: DEDR 4395(a) explicitly gives Kannada heṅgasu female, Malayalam peṇ girl/female and Tulu poṇjavu/poṇjevu woman; Tamil peṇ/peṇṭu is the corresponding family. Survey Tamil poṇṇə is a comparative colloquial variant marked as a look-alike by the upstream source, not a literal DEDR citation. Longer compound responses are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 5517 explicitly gives Kannada beṅki fire, Malto béru sun, Brahui bāsing become hot and Ollari Gadaba veytal hot (in veytal nīr hot water). The source annotation identifies the family; survey benki, bērdu, bāsun and veṭal preserve their consonant and ending differences. The Gadaba survey response is the heat word alone, so no water component is inferred. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR497 directly gives Kannada ele/ela, Kota el, Toda es̱ and Tulu irè/ele leaf. Survey yele, ēlu, ers and ira preserve the initial glide, final-vowel and Toda sibilant transcription differences; full article and source cognacy support the same leaf family. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

Badaga oṭṭe is a comparative extension marked as a look-alike; its missing initial consonant remains visible for review. Malto puḍā preserves its stop transcription. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
